claim: More than 10% of the mouse genome is made up of endogenous retroviruses (ERVs).
source: More than 10% of the mouse genome is made up of endogenous retroviruses (ERVs) (Smit et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Smit et al., 2015

claim: ERVs contain retrotransposition-enabling genes flanked by non-coding identical 5′ and 3′ long terminal repeats (LTRs).
source: ERVs are transposable elements (TEs) containing retrotransposition-enabling genes flanked by non-coding identical 5′ and 3′ long terminal repeats (LTRs).
evidence: Established scientific knowledge about ERV structure

claim: Most ERVs have lost their mobilisation potential due to mutational decay.
source: Although most ERVs have lost their mobilisation potential due to mutational decay, they retain the ability to modulate host genome function through the use of transcriptional regulation motifs contained in their sequences.
evidence: Established scientific knowledge about ERV evolution

claim: ERVs retain the ability to modulate host genome function through transcriptional regulation motifs.
source: Although most ERVs have lost their mobilisation potential due to mutational decay, they retain the ability to modulate host genome function through the use of transcriptional regulation motifs contained in their sequences.
evidence: Established scientific knowledge about ERV function

claim: ERV sequences contain transcription factor binding sites, polyadenylation signals, and splice acceptor sites.
source: These include transcription factor binding sites, polyadenylation signals, and splice acceptor sites (Maksakova et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to Maksakova et al., 2006

claim: Solo LTRs are produced via inter-LTR homologous recombination.
source: For instance, solo LTRs produced via inter-LTR homologous recombination make up a large fraction of mammalian ERV sequences and can influence host gene expression through their promoter activity (Nellåker et al., 2012; Ruda et al., 2004; Subramanian et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Nellåker et al., 2012; Ruda et al., 2004; Subramanian et al., 2011

claim: Solo LTRs make up a large fraction of mammalian ERV sequences.
source: For instance, solo LTRs produced via inter-LTR homologous recombination make up a large fraction of mammalian ERV sequences and can influence host gene expression through their promoter activity (Nellåker et al., 2012; Ruda et al., 2004; Subramanian et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Nellåker et al., 2012; Ruda et al., 2004; Subramanian et al., 2011

claim: Solo LTRs can influence host gene expression through their promoter activity.
source: For instance, solo LTRs produced via inter-LTR homologous recombination make up a large fraction of mammalian ERV sequences and can influence host gene expression through their promoter activity (Nellåker et al., 2012; Ruda et al., 2004; Subramanian et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Nellåker et al., 2012; Ruda et al., 2004; Subramanian et al., 2011

claim: The vast majority of mouse ERVs exhibit high levels of DNA methylation.
source: The vast majority of mouse ERVs exhibit high levels of DNA methylation, and loss of DNA methyltransferase activity causes an increase in ERV transcription in embryos and in the germline (Barau et al., 2016; Bourc'his and Bestor, 2004; Jain et al., 2017; Walsh et al., 1998).
evidence: Supported by citations to Barau et al., 2016; Bourc'his and Bestor, 2004; Jain et al., 2017; Walsh et al., 1998

claim: Loss of DNA methyltransferase activity causes an increase in ERV transcription in embryos and in the germline.
source: The vast majority of mouse ERVs exhibit high levels of DNA methylation, and loss of DNA methyltransferase activity causes an increase in ERV transcription in embryos and in the germline (Barau et al., 2016; Bourc'his and Bestor, 2004; Jain et al., 2017; Walsh et al., 1998).
evidence: Supported by citations to Barau et al., 2016; Bourc'his and Bestor, 2004; Jain et al., 2017; Walsh et al., 1998

claim: The deposition of histone H3 lysine nine trimethylation (H3K9me3) by the methyltransferase SETDB1 in early development is crucial for ERV repression.
source: In addition, the deposition of histone H3 lysine nine trimethylation (H3K9me3) by the methyltransferase SETDB1 (or ESET) in early development is crucial for ERV repression (Matsui et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Matsui et al., 2010

claim: SETDB1 is recruited to ERVs following the binding of KAP1 to KRAB zinc finger proteins (KZFPs) that recognise specific sequence motifs within ERV elements.
source: SETDB1 is recruited to ERVs following the binding of KAP1 (or TRIM28) to KRAB zinc finger proteins (KZFPs) that recognise specific sequence motifs within ERV elements (Ecco et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ecco et al., 2017

claim: RNA-mediated mechanisms such as the piRNA pathway play key roles in silencing mammalian ERVs, especially in the male germline.
source: RNA-mediated mechanisms such as the piRNA pathway also play key roles in silencing mammalian ERVs, especially in the male germline (Aravin et al., 2007; Carmell et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to Aravin et al., 2007; Carmell et al., 2007

claim: Intracisternal A-particles (IAPs) are murine-specific ERVs.
source: Intracisternal A-particles (IAPs) are murine-specific ERVs.
evidence: Established scientific knowledge about IAPs

claim: IAPs are young and highly active elements.
source: They are young and highly active elements, exhibiting extensive insertional polymorphism across inbred mouse strains and accounting for more than 10,000 ERVs in the C57BL/6J (B6) inbred strain (Nellåker et al., 2012; Smit et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Nellåker et al., 2012; Smit et al., 2015

claim: IAPs exhibit extensive insertional polymorphism across inbred mouse strains.
source: They are young and highly active elements, exhibiting extensive insertional polymorphism across inbred mouse strains and accounting for more than 10,000 ERVs in the C57BL/6J (B6) inbred strain (Nellåker et al., 2012; Smit et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Nellåker et al., 2012; Smit et al., 2015

claim: IAPs account for more than 10,000 ERVs in the C57BL/6J (B6) inbred strain.
source: They are young and highly active elements, exhibiting extensive insertional polymorphism across inbred mouse strains and accounting for more than 10,000 ERVs in the C57BL/6J (B6) inbred strain (Nellåker et al., 2012; Smit et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Nellåker et al., 2012; Smit et al., 2015

claim: IAP insertions are responsible for the majority of documented insertional mutations in the mouse.
source: IAP insertions are responsible for the majority of documented insertional mutations in the mouse, most of which disrupt host gene function by generating aberrant or fusion gene transcripts (Gagnier et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gagnier et al., 2019

claim: Most IAP insertional mutations disrupt host gene function by generating aberrant or fusion gene transcripts.
source: IAP insertions are responsible for the majority of documented insertional mutations in the mouse, most of which disrupt host gene function by generating aberrant or fusion gene transcripts (Gagnier et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gagnier et al., 2019

claim: In some cases, the phenotypic severity of IAP mutations is associated with the methylation status of the IAP.
source: In some cases, the phenotypic severity of the mutation is associated with the methylation status of the IAP.
evidence: General statement supported by the Avy example that follows

claim: The IAP LTR promoter at the Agouti viable yellow (Avy) allele drives ectopic expression of the downstream coat colour gene Agouti when unmethylated.
source: For example, the IAP LTR promoter at the Agouti viable yellow (Avy) allele drives ectopic expression of the downstream coat colour gene Agouti when unmethylated.
evidence: Established knowledge about the Avy allele

claim: The Avy IAP exhibits variable DNA methylation levels across genetically identical individuals.
source: By mechanisms not yet fully understood, the Avy IAP exhibits variable DNA methylation levels across genetically identical individuals, which results in inbred mice displaying a range of coat colours (Duhl et al., 1994; Morgan et al., 1999).
evidence: Supported by citations to Duhl et al., 1994; Morgan et al., 1999

claim: Variable DNA methylation at the Avy IAP results in inbred mice displaying a range of coat colours.
source: By mechanisms not yet fully understood, the Avy IAP exhibits variable DNA methylation levels across genetically identical individuals, which results in inbred mice displaying a range of coat colours (Duhl et al., 1994; Morgan et al., 1999).
evidence: Supported by citations to Duhl et al., 1994; Morgan et al., 1999

claim: A genome-wide screen identified dozens of novel variably methylated IAPs (VM-IAPs) in the B6 genome.
source: We identified dozens of novel variably methylated IAPs (VM-IAPs) in the B6 genome and showed that their characteristic methylation variability is recapitulated from generation to generation irrespective of parental methylation level.
evidence: Supported by references to previous work by the authors (Elmer et al., 2021; Kazachenka et al., 2018)

claim: VM-IAP methylation variability is recapitulated from generation to generation irrespective of parental methylation level.
source: We identified dozens of novel variably methylated IAPs (VM-IAPs) in the B6 genome and showed that their characteristic methylation variability is recapitulated from generation to generation irrespective of parental methylation level.
evidence: Supported by references to previous work by the authors (Elmer et al., 2021; Kazachenka et al., 2018)

claim: The screen for VM-IAPs identified the IAP-Pgm2 element.
source: Our screen for VM-IAPs identified the IAP-Pgm2 element, named after its closest annotated coding gene Phosphoglucomutase-2 (Pgm2).
evidence: Reported finding from the authors' previous screen

claim: IAP-Pgm2 is a fully structured 7.5 kb IAP located on Chromosome 5.
source: It is a fully structured 7.5 kb IAP located on Chromosome 5 containing identical 5′ and 3′ LTRs of the IAPLTR2_Mm subclass (mm10 coordinates: chr5:64,030,834–64,038,297; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Characterization data from the study

claim: IAP-Pgm2 contains identical 5′ and 3′ LTRs of the IAPLTR2_Mm subclass.
source: It is a fully structured 7.5 kb IAP located on Chromosome 5 containing identical 5′ and 3′ LTRs of the IAPLTR2_Mm subclass (mm10 coordinates: chr5:64,030,834–64,038,297; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Characterization data from the study

claim: IAP-Pgm2 exhibits two distinct DNA methylation states which are stably inherited from parent to offspring within the B6 strain.
source: Here we show that IAP-Pgm2, in sharp contrast to VM-IAPs, exhibits two distinct DNA methylation states which are stably inherited from parent to offspring within the B6 strain.
evidence: Main finding of the study supported by experimental data

claim: The epiallele at IAP-Pgm2 is genetically conferred.
source: Sequencing of the locus reveals that the epiallele is genetically conferred, where the methylated variant of IAP-Pgm2 is a full-length IAP matching the B6 reference genome (renamed Iap5-1full) and the unmethylated variant is a solo LTR produced from an inter-LTR recombination event (renamed Iap5-1solo).
evidence: Main finding of the study supported by sequencing data

claim: The methylated variant of IAP-Pgm2 is a full-length IAP matching the B6 reference genome.
source: Sequencing of the locus reveals that the epiallele is genetically conferred, where the methylated variant of IAP-Pgm2 is a full-length IAP matching the B6 reference genome (renamed Iap5-1full) and the unmethylated variant is a solo LTR produced from an inter-LTR recombination event (renamed Iap5-1solo).
evidence: Main finding of the study supported by sequencing data

claim: The unmethylated variant of IAP-Pgm2 is a solo LTR produced from an inter-LTR recombination event.
source: Sequencing of the locus reveals that the epiallele is genetically conferred, where the methylated variant of IAP-Pgm2 is a full-length IAP matching the B6 reference genome (renamed Iap5-1full) and the unmethylated variant is a solo LTR produced from an inter-LTR recombination event (renamed Iap5-1solo).
evidence: Main finding of the study supported by sequencing data

claim: The absence of DNA methylation at Iap5-1solo is accompanied by a loss of H3K9me3 marks.
source: The absence of DNA methylation at Iap5-1solo is accompanied by a loss of H3K9me3 marks.
evidence: Main finding of the study supported by ChIP-qPCR data

claim: Differential modification of the two Iap5-1 variants is established during early preimplantation development.
source: We find that differential modification of the two variants is established during early preimplantation development and identify candidate KZFPs responsible for the acquisition of contrasting epigenetic states.
evidence: Main finding of the study supported by developmental time course data

claim: Candidate KZFPs are responsible for the acquisition of contrasting epigenetic states at Iap5-1.
source: We find that differential modification of the two variants is established during early preimplantation development and identify candidate KZFPs responsible for the acquisition of contrasting epigenetic states.
evidence: Main finding of the study supported by ChIP-seq analysis

claim: Iap5-1solo is unresponsive to dietary methyl supplementation.
source: We report that Iap5-1solo is unresponsive to dietary methyl supplementation but highly susceptible to genetic background, becoming a bona fide VM-IAP in an F1 hybrid context.
evidence: Main finding of the study supported by dietary intervention experiment

claim: Iap5-1solo is highly susceptible to genetic background.
source: We report that Iap5-1solo is unresponsive to dietary methyl supplementation but highly susceptible to genetic background, becoming a bona fide VM-IAP in an F1 hybrid context.
evidence: Main finding of the study supported by hybrid cross experiments

claim: Iap5-1solo becomes a bona fide VM-IAP in an F1 hybrid context.
source: We report that Iap5-1solo is unresponsive to dietary methyl supplementation but highly susceptible to genetic background, becoming a bona fide VM-IAP in an F1 hybrid context.
evidence: Main finding of the study supported by hybrid cross experiments

claim: Differential epigenetic modification of the two Iap5-1 variants is associated with metabolic differences.
source: Differential epigenetic modification of the two variants is associated with metabolic differences and tissue-specific changes in adjacent gene expression.
evidence: Main finding of the study supported by metabolic assays

claim: Differential epigenetic modification of the two Iap5-1 variants is associated with tissue-specific changes in adjacent gene expression.
source: Differential epigenetic modification of the two variants is associated with metabolic differences and tissue-specific changes in adjacent gene expression.
evidence: Main finding of the study supported by RT-qPCR data

claim: IAP-Pgm2 5′ LTR exhibited three distinct states: high (>85%), low (<20%), and intermediate (60–70%) methylation.
source: While VM-IAP DNA methylation levels display continuous probability distributions in the B6 population, the IAP-Pgm2 5′ LTR exhibited three distinct states: high (>85%), low (<20%), and intermediate (60–70%) methylation (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: Experimental observation from bisulphite pyrosequencing data shown in Figure 1A and B

claim: The tri-modal methylation pattern at IAP-Pgm2 was observed in both sexes.
source: This pattern was observed in both sexes (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Experimental observation shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2

claim: 5′ and 3′ LTR methylation levels at IAP-Pgm2 were consistent with one another within an individual.
source: In addition, 5′ and 3′ LTR methylation levels were consistent with one another within an individual (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: Experimental observation from bisulphite pyrosequencing data shown in Figure 1A and B

claim: The three distinct methylation states at IAP-Pgm2 become less defined as the distance from the LTR borders increases.
source: Methylation quantification of unique non-repetitive DNA immediately up- and downstream of IAP-Pgm2 showed that the three distinct methylation states become less defined as the distance from the LTR borders increases, ultimately collapsing approximately 500 bp from either side of the IAP (Figure 1C).
evidence: Experimental observation from bisulphite pyrosequencing data shown in Figure 1C

claim: The three distinct methylation states at IAP-Pgm2 collapse approximately 500 bp from either side of the IAP.
source: Methylation quantification of unique non-repetitive DNA immediately up- and downstream of IAP-Pgm2 showed that the three distinct methylation states become less defined as the distance from the LTR borders increases, ultimately collapsing approximately 500 bp from either side of the IAP (Figure 1C).
evidence: Experimental observation from bisulphite pyrosequencing data shown in Figure 1C

claim: The methylation differences observed between individuals at IAP-Pgm2 are intrinsic to the IAP-Pgm2 element rather than a reflection of differential methylation of the insertion site prior to integration.
source: This provides evidence for short-distance spreading of DNA methylation levels from IAP-Pgm2 into bordering DNA and suggests that the methylation differences observed between individuals are intrinsic to the IAP-Pgm2 element rather than a reflection of differential methylation of the insertion site prior to integration.
evidence: Inference based on the spreading pattern observed in Figure 1C

claim: Offspring born to highly methylated IAP-Pgm2 parents were all highly methylated.
source: Offspring born to highly methylated parents were all highly methylated and offspring born to lowly methylated parents were all lowly methylated (Figure 1D).
evidence: Experimental observation from breeding experiments shown in Figure 1D

claim: Offspring born to lowly methylated IAP-Pgm2 parents were all lowly methylated.
source: Offspring born to highly methylated parents were all highly methylated and offspring born to lowly methylated parents were all lowly methylated (Figure 1D).
evidence: Experimental observation from breeding experiments shown in Figure 1D

claim: When one IAP-Pgm2 parent was highly methylated and the other lowly methylated, all offspring were intermediately methylated.
source: When one parent was highly methylated and the other lowly methylated, all offspring were intermediately methylated (Figure 1D).
evidence: Experimental observation from breeding experiments shown in Figure 1D

claim: High and low methylation states at IAP-Pgm2 are allelic variants.
source: This indicates that high and low methylation states are allelic variants of IAP-Pgm2 (designated IAP-Pgm2HH and IAP-Pgm2LL), with intermediate methylation representing co-dominant epigenetic heterozygosity (IAP-Pgm2HL).
evidence: Inference based on Mendelian inheritance pattern observed in breeding experiments

claim: Intermediate methylation at IAP-Pgm2 represents co-dominant epigenetic heterozygosity.
source: This indicates that high and low methylation states are allelic variants of IAP-Pgm2 (designated IAP-Pgm2HH and IAP-Pgm2LL), with intermediate methylation representing co-dominant epigenetic heterozygosity (IAP-Pgm2HL).
evidence: Inference based on Mendelian inheritance pattern observed in breeding experiments

claim: An IAP-Pgm2HL intercross produced IAP-Pgm2HH, IAP-Pgm2LL, and IAP-Pgm2HL offspring.
source: Additional crosses confirmed this inheritance pattern: an IAP-Pgm2HL intercross produced IAP-Pgm2HH, IAP-Pgm2LL, and IAP-Pgm2HL offspring; an IAP-Pgm2HH x IAP-Pgm2HL cross produced IAP-Pgm2HH and IAP-Pgm2HL offspring; and an IAP-Pgm2LL x IAP-Pgm2HL cross produced IAP-Pgm2LL and IAP-Pgm2HL offspring (Figure 1D).
evidence: Experimental observation from breeding experiments shown in Figure 1D

claim: An IAP-Pgm2HH x IAP-Pgm2HL cross produced IAP-Pgm2HH and IAP-Pgm2HL offspring.
source: Additional crosses confirmed this inheritance pattern: an IAP-Pgm2HL intercross produced IAP-Pgm2HH, IAP-Pgm2LL, and IAP-Pgm2HL offspring; an IAP-Pgm2HH x IAP-Pgm2HL cross produced IAP-Pgm2HH and IAP-Pgm2HL offspring; and an IAP-Pgm2LL x IAP-Pgm2HL cross produced IAP-Pgm2LL and IAP-Pgm2HL offspring (Figure 1D).
evidence: Experimental observation from breeding experiments shown in Figure 1D

claim: An IAP-Pgm2LL x IAP-Pgm2HL cross produced IAP-Pgm2LL and IAP-Pgm2HL offspring.
source: Additional crosses confirmed this inheritance pattern: an IAP-Pgm2HL intercross produced IAP-Pgm2HH, IAP-Pgm2LL, and IAP-Pgm2HL offspring; an IAP-Pgm2HH x IAP-Pgm2HL cross produced IAP-Pgm2HH and IAP-Pgm2HL offspring; and an IAP-Pgm2LL x IAP-Pgm2HL cross produced IAP-Pgm2LL and IAP-Pgm2HL offspring (Figure 1D).
evidence: Experimental observation from breeding experiments shown in Figure 1D

claim: The methylation state of one IAP-Pgm2 variant does not influence the methylation state of the other in a heterozygous context.
source: These results additionally demonstrate that the methylation state of one IAP-Pgm2 variant does not influence the methylation state of the other in a heterozygous context.
evidence: Inference based on the independent segregation observed in breeding experiments

claim: Nested primer pairs N1 and N2 amplified two overlapping fragments from IAP-Pgm2HH gDNA, each containing half of the IAP-Pgm2 element.
source: Agarose gel electrophoresis of the PCR products revealed amplification of both fragments from IAP-Pgm2HH gDNA but no amplification of either fragment from IAP-Pgm2LL gDNA (Figure 2B and C), pointing to a substantial genetic difference between IAP-Pgm2HH and IAP-Pgm2LL individuals.
evidence: Experimental observation from PCR and gel electrophoresis shown in Figure 2B and C

claim: Nested primer pairs N1 and N2 did not amplify any fragments from IAP-Pgm2LL gDNA.
source: Agarose gel electrophoresis of the PCR products revealed amplification of both fragments from IAP-Pgm2HH gDNA but no amplification of either fragment from IAP-Pgm2LL gDNA (Figure 2B and C), pointing to a substantial genetic difference between IAP-Pgm2HH and IAP-Pgm2LL individuals.
evidence: Experimental observation from PCR and gel electrophoresis shown in Figure 2B and C

claim: There is a substantial genetic difference between IAP-Pgm2HH and IAP-Pgm2LL individuals.
source: Agarose gel electrophoresis of the PCR products revealed amplification of both fragments from IAP-Pgm2HH gDNA but no amplification of either fragment from IAP-Pgm2LL gDNA (Figure 2B and C), pointing to a substantial genetic difference between IAP-Pgm2HH and IAP-Pgm2LL individuals.
evidence: Inference based on differential PCR amplification patterns

claim: No DNA bands were observed following the use of primer pair N3 on IAP-Pgm2HH gDNA.
source: While no DNA bands were observed following the use of this primer pair on IAP-Pgm2HH gDNA, a 1.5 kb band was amplified from both IAP-Pgm2LL and IAP-Pgm2HL gDNA (Figure 2D).
evidence: Experimental observation from PCR and gel electrophoresis shown in Figure 2D

claim: A 1.5 kb band was amplified from both IAP-Pgm2LL and IAP-Pgm2HL gDNA using primer pair N3.
source: While no DNA bands were observed following the use of this primer pair on IAP-Pgm2HH gDNA, a 1.5 kb band was amplified from both IAP-Pgm2LL and IAP-Pgm2HL gDNA (Figure 2D).
evidence: Experimental observation from PCR and gel electrophoresis shown in Figure 2D

claim: The smaller amplicon from primer pair N3 is indicative of a 7 kb deletion on the IAP-Pgm2L allele between the two primer annealing sites.
source: The smaller amplicon is indicative of a 7 kb deletion on the IAP-Pgm2L allele between the two primer annealing sites, while the lack of amplification from the IAP-Pgm2H allele is likely due to the technical challenges associated with amplifying a large repetitive DNA fragment.
evidence: Inference based on the size difference between expected and observed amplicons

claim: The lack of amplification from the IAP-Pgm2H allele using primer pair N3 is likely due to the technical challenges associated with amplifying a large repetitive DNA fragment.
source: The smaller amplicon is indicative of a 7 kb deletion on the IAP-Pgm2L allele between the two primer annealing sites, while the lack of amplification from the IAP-Pgm2H allele is likely due to the technical challenges associated with amplifying a large repetitive DNA fragment.
evidence: Speculation based on known technical limitations of PCR

claim: The IAP-Pgm2H allele is an identical match to the full-length IAP-Pgm2 sequence from the mm10 reference.
source: The alignment revealed that the IAP-Pgm2H allele is an identical match to the full-length IAP-Pgm2 sequence from the mm10 reference, while the IAP-Pgm2L allele is a solo LTR (Figure 2E).
evidence: Experimental observation from Sanger sequencing and alignment shown in Figure 2E

claim: The IAP-Pgm2L allele is a solo LTR.
source: The alignment revealed that the IAP-Pgm2H allele is an identical match to the full-length IAP-Pgm2 sequence from the mm10 reference, while the IAP-Pgm2L allele is a solo LTR (Figure 2E).
evidence: Experimental observation from Sanger sequencing and alignment shown in Figure 2E

claim: The IAP-Pgm2L solo LTR and the IAP-Pgm2H full-length IAP are both flanked by the same target site duplications (TSDs).
source: The IAP-Pgm2L solo LTR and the IAP-Pgm2H full-length IAP are both flanked by the same target site duplications (TSDs) and the IAP-Pgm2L solo LTR exhibits 100% sequence identity to both the 5′ and 3′ LTRs of the full-length IAP-Pgm2H (Figure 2E).
evidence: Experimental observation from Sanger sequencing and alignment shown in Figure 2E

claim: The IAP-Pgm2L solo LTR exhibits 100% sequence identity to both the 5′ and 3′ LTRs of the full-length IAP-Pgm2H.
source: The IAP-Pgm2L solo LTR and the IAP-Pgm2H full-length IAP are both flanked by the same target site duplications (TSDs) and the IAP-Pgm2L solo LTR exhibits 100% sequence identity to both the 5′ and 3′ LTRs of the full-length IAP-Pgm2H (Figure 2E).
evidence: Experimental observation from Sanger sequencing and alignment shown in Figure 2E

claim: A recent inter-LTR homologous recombination event in the inbred B6 mouse strain gave rise to the solo LTR variant.
source: Therefore, a recent inter-LTR homologous recombination event in the inbred B6 mouse strain gave rise to the solo LTR variant.
evidence: Inference based on the sequence identity and structural features observed

claim: Inter-LTR recombination events occur when identical or near-identical LTR sequences engage in ectopic homologous recombination, resulting in the formation of solo LTRs.
source: Inter-LTR recombination events occur when identical or near-identical LTR sequences engage in ectopic homologous recombination, resulting in the formation of solo LTRs (Jern and Coffin, 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Jern and Coffin, 2008

claim: Both Iap5-1 allelic variants were identified in B6 samples from mainland Europe and North America.
source: Although we identified both Iap5-1 allelic variants in our own B6 colony, we also detected them in B6 samples sent to us from mainland Europe and North America (data not shown), so the recombination event most likely occurred at a B6-distributing facility.
evidence: Experimental observation from genotyping samples from different sources

claim: The recombination event that gave rise to Iap5-1solo most likely occurred at a B6-distributing facility.
source: Although we identified both Iap5-1 allelic variants in our own B6 colony, we also detected them in B6 samples sent to us from mainland Europe and North America (data not shown), so the recombination event most likely occurred at a B6-distributing facility.
evidence: Inference based on the widespread distribution of both alleles

claim: Approximately half of the IAPs in the mouse genome are solo LTRs.
source: This type of proviral excision event is common: approximately half of the IAPs in the mouse genome are solo LTRs (Nellåker et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Nellåker et al., 2012

claim: The vast majority of the ~5,000 solo LTRs in the B6 genome are highly methylated.
source: However, the vast majority of the ~5,000 solo LTRs in the B6 genome are highly methylated (Shimosuga et al., 2017), making Iap5-1solo unique from a regulatory perspective and raising questions regarding the functional consequences of a solo LTR left unmodified.
evidence: Supported by citation to Shimosuga et al., 2017

claim: Iap5-1solo is unique from a regulatory perspective among solo LTRs in the B6 genome.
source: However, the vast majority of the ~5,000 solo LTRs in the B6 genome are highly methylated (Shimosuga et al., 2017), making Iap5-1solo unique from a regulatory perspective and raising questions regarding the functional consequences of a solo LTR left unmodified.
evidence: Inference based on comparison with other solo LTRs

claim: The entirety of the Iap5-1solo solo LTR is unmethylated (bar the occasional methylated CpGs at the 5′ end).
source: Using clonal bisulphite sequencing, we confirmed that the entirety of the Iap5-1solo solo LTR is unmethylated (bar the occasional methylated CpGs at the 5′ end, consistent with the pyrosequencing data) while all CpGs in both the 5′ and 3′ LTRs of Iap5-1full are highly methylated (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Experimental observation from clonal bisulphite sequencing shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2

claim: All CpGs in both the 5′ and 3′ LTRs of Iap5-1full are highly methylated.
source: Using clonal bisulphite sequencing, we confirmed that the entirety of the Iap5-1solo solo LTR is unmethylated (bar the occasional methylated CpGs at the 5′ end, consistent with the pyrosequencing data) while all CpGs in both the 5′ and 3′ LTRs of Iap5-1full are highly methylated (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Experimental observation from clonal bisulphite sequencing shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2

claim: Oocytes collected from Iap5-1full females were highly methylated at the Iap5-1 locus.
source: Oocytes collected from Iap5-1full and Iap5-1solo females were highly and lowly methylated at the Iap5-1 locus, respectively (Figure 2F).
evidence: Experimental observation from bisulphite pyrosequencing of oocytes shown in Figure 2F

claim: Oocytes collected from Iap5-1solo females were lowly methylated at the Iap5-1 locus.
source: Oocytes collected from Iap5-1full and Iap5-1solo females were highly and lowly methylated at the Iap5-1 locus, respectively (Figure 2F).
evidence: Experimental observation from bisulphite pyrosequencing of oocytes shown in Figure 2F

claim: Oocyte Iap5-1 methylation levels are reflective of somatic Iap5-1 methylation levels.
source: Thus, oocyte Iap5-1 methylation levels are reflective of somatic Iap5-1 methylation levels.
evidence: Inference based on comparison of oocyte and somatic methylation data

claim: Both Iap5-1 variants were hypermethylated in sperm.
source: In contrast, both variants were hypermethylated in sperm (Figure 2F), indicating that both alleles are targeted for repression during spermatogenesis by mechanism(s) that are distinct from those operating on Iap5-1 in the soma.
evidence: Experimental observation from bisulphite pyrosequencing of sperm shown in Figure 2F

claim: Both Iap5-1 alleles are targeted for repression during spermatogenesis by mechanism(s) that are distinct from those operating on Iap5-1 in the soma.
source: In contrast, both variants were hypermethylated in sperm (Figure 2F), indicating that both alleles are targeted for repression during spermatogenesis by mechanism(s) that are distinct from those operating on Iap5-1 in the soma.
evidence: Inference based on the differential methylation patterns between sperm and soma

claim: The maternal and paternal Iap5-1solo alleles are differentially methylated upon fertilisation in the early zygote.
source: Together, these experiments indicate that the maternal and paternal Iap5-1solo alleles are differentially methylated upon fertilisation in the early zygote.
evidence: Inference based on the differential methylation in oocytes and sperm

claim: Blastocysts generated from Iap5-1solo parents exhibited low methylation levels at Iap5-1.
source: Blastocysts generated from Iap5-1solo parents exhibited low methylation levels at Iap5-1, suggesting that the paternally inherited hypermethylated Iap5-1solo allele becomes demethylated shortly after fertilisation (Figure 2F).
evidence: Experimental observation from bisulphite pyrosequencing of blastocysts shown in Figure 2F

claim: The paternally inherited hypermethylated Iap5-1solo allele becomes demethylated shortly after fertilisation.
source: Blastocysts generated from Iap5-1solo parents exhibited low methylation levels at Iap5-1, suggesting that the paternally inherited hypermethylated Iap5-1solo allele becomes demethylated shortly after fertilisation (Figure 2F).
evidence: Inference based on the low methylation observed in blastocysts despite high paternal methylation

claim: Blastocysts generated from Iap5-1full parents exhibited methylation levels around 70%.
source: By comparison, blastocysts generated from Iap5-1full parents exhibited methylation levels around 70% (Figure 2F).
evidence: Experimental observation from bisulphite pyrosequencing of blastocysts shown in Figure 2F

claim: Methylation patterns at Iap5-1full and Iap5-1solo are specified prior to implantation.
source: Nonetheless, these results demonstrate that methylation patterns at Iap5-1full and Iap5-1solo are specified prior to implantation.
evidence: Inference based on the distinct methylation patterns observed in blastocysts

claim: DNA methylation levels in embryonic stem (ES) cell lines derived from the ICM of Iap5-1full and Iap5-1solo blastocysts closely matched those observed in adult somatic tissues.
source: In support of this, DNA methylation levels in embryonic stem (ES) cell lines derived from the ICM of Iap5-1full and Iap5-1solo blastocysts closely matched those observed in adult somatic tissues, with ES cells derived from Iap5-1full blastocysts nearing 100% methylation (Figure 2F).
evidence: Experimental observation from bisulphite pyrosequencing of ES cells shown in Figure 2F

claim: ES cells derived from Iap5-1full blastocysts nearing 100% methylation.
source: In support of this, DNA methylation levels in embryonic stem (ES) cell lines derived from the ICM of Iap5-1full and Iap5-1solo blastocysts closely matched those observed in adult somatic tissues, with ES cells derived from Iap5-1full blastocysts nearing 100% methylation (Figure 2F).
evidence: Experimental observation from bisulphite pyrosequencing of ES cells shown in Figure 2F

claim: Iap5-1full methylation levels in E16.5 placentas were lower than those in E16.5 embryonic tissue.
source: In addition, we found that Iap5-1full methylation levels in E16.5 placentas were lower than those in E16.5 embryonic tissue (Figure 2F), consistent with reduced global DNA methylation in the placenta (Ehrlich et al., 1982; Schroeder et al., 2015).
evidence: Experimental observation from bisulphite pyrosequencing of E16.5 samples shown in Figure 2F

claim: The two Iap5-1 variants retain a pronounced difference in DNA methylation levels in placental tissue.
source: Of note, even though placental Iap5-1 methylation levels are less methylated compared to their embryonic counterparts, the two variants retain a pronounced difference in DNA methylation levels in this tissue.
evidence: Inference based on the methylation data from placental samples

claim: H3K9me3 enrichment at the 5′ and the 3′ borders was significantly decreased in Iap5-1solo samples compared to Iap5-1full samples.
source: H3K9me3 enrichment at the 5′ and the 3′ borders was significantly decreased in Iap5-1solo samples compared to Iap5-1full samples (Figure 3A).
evidence: Experimental observation from ChIP-qPCR shown in Figure 3A

claim: Iap5-1full showed comparable H3K9me3 levels to those observed at the positive controls IAP-Asxl3 and SINE-Rbak.
source: Iap5-1full showed comparable H3K9me3 levels to those observed at the positive controls (Figure 3A).
evidence: Experimental observation from ChIP-qPCR shown in Figure 3A

claim: The slightly higher H3K9me3 enrichment at the 3′ end compared to the 5′ end in Iap5-1solo samples is due to the presence of an ERV element immediately downstream of Iap5-1.
source: We suggest that the slightly higher H3K9me3 enrichment at the 3′ end compared to the 5′ end in Iap5-1solo samples is due to the presence of an ERV element immediately downstream of Iap5-1.
evidence: Speculation based on the genomic context

claim: Iap5-1full may be targeted for repression in the early embryo by KZFP(s) whose binding sites are located in the internal proviral portion of the IAP which is no longer present in the Iap5-1solo variant.
source: We reasoned that Iap5-1full may be targeted for repression in the early embryo by KZFP(s) whose binding sites are located in the internal proviral portion of the IAP which is no longer present in the Iap5-1solo variant.
evidence: Speculation based on the structural differences between the two variants

claim: Two Iap5-1full-binding KZFP candidates were identified: Gm14419 and Gm8898.
source: To explore this hypothesis, we analysed previously published ChIP-seq (chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by high-throughput sequencing) binding profiles of more than 60 murine KZFPs (Wolf et al., 2020) and identified two Iap5-1full-binding candidates, Gm14419 and Gm8898 (Figure 3B).
evidence: Analysis of published ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3B

claim: The ChIP-seq profiles for Gm14419 and Gm8898 in B6 ES cells displayed peaks immediately downstream and 1.5 kb downstream of the 5′ LTR, respectively.
source: The ChIP-seq profiles for Gm14419 and Gm8898 in B6 ES cells displayed peaks immediately downstream and 1.5 kb downstream of the 5′ LTR, respectively (Figure 3B).
evidence: Analysis of published ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3B

claim: KAP1 occupancy was observed at the Gm14419 binding site.
source: We observed KAP1 occupancy at the Gm14419 binding site, rendering Gm14419 a particularly promising candidate for future mechanistic research (Figure 3B).
evidence: Analysis of published ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3B

claim: Gm14419 is a particularly promising candidate for future mechanistic research.
source: We observed KAP1 occupancy at the Gm14419 binding site, rendering Gm14419 a particularly promising candidate for future mechanistic research (Figure 3B).
evidence: Inference based on the KAP1 occupancy at the Gm14419 binding site

claim: The Gm14419 peak overlaps with the primer binding site (PBS) just downstream of the 5′ LTR.
source: The Gm14419 peak overlaps with the primer binding site (PBS) just downstream of the 5′ LTR (Figure 3B), a retroviral sequence often bound by KZFPs to effectuate repression (Wolf and Goff, 2007).
evidence: Analysis of published ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3B

claim: The primer binding site (PBS) is a retroviral sequence often bound by KZFPs to effectuate repression.
source: The Gm14419 peak overlaps with the primer binding site (PBS) just downstream of the 5′ LTR (Figure 3B), a retroviral sequence often bound by KZFPs to effectuate repression (Wolf and Goff, 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wolf and Goff, 2007

claim: It is likely that additional as yet unidentified KZFP(s) bind to Iap5-1full.
source: Furthermore, it is likely that additional as yet unidentified KZFP(s) bind to Iap5-1full, as evidenced by a second KAP1 peak in the Iap5-1full internal region which does not overlap with the binding site of any of the KZFPs identified in our analysis (Figure 3B).
evidence: Inference based on the presence of a KAP1 peak without a corresponding KZFP peak

claim: A second KAP1 peak in the Iap5-1full internal region does not overlap with the binding site of any of the KZFPs identified in the analysis.
source: Furthermore, it is likely that additional as yet unidentified KZFP(s) bind to Iap5-1full, as evidenced by a second KAP1 peak in the Iap5-1full internal region which does not overlap with the binding site of any of the KZFPs identified in our analysis (Figure 3B).
evidence: Analysis of published ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3B

claim: The observation of a KAP1 peak without a corresponding KZFP peak is consistent with the redundant nature of KZFP-mediated ERV repression.
source: This is consistent with the redundant nature of KZFP-mediated ERV repression (Imbeault et al., 2017; Wolf et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Imbeault et al., 2017; Wolf et al., 2020

claim: ZFP429 binding peaks were detected at the 5′ and 3′ LTRs of Iap5-1full.
source: In addition, we detected ZFP429 binding peaks at the 5′ and 3′ LTRs of Iap5-1full (Figure 3B).
evidence: Analysis of published ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3B

claim: ZFP429 does not recruit heterochromatin factors as effectively as other KZFPs.
source: Given the shared sequence between the Iap5-1full LTRs and Iap5-1solo, this observation suggests that ZFP429 does not recruit heterochromatin factors as effectively as other KZFPs.
evidence: Inference based on the presence of ZFP429 binding at both variants despite differential methylation

claim: ZFP429 is enriched at VM-IAPs compared to fully methylated IAPs of the same subclass.
source: This is in line with our previous finding that ZFP429 is enriched at VM-IAPs compared to fully methylated IAPs of the same subclass (Bertozzi et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work by the authors (Bertozzi et al., 2020)

claim: Hemizygous offspring born to a Iap5-1full B6 parent were highly methylated.
source: In line with our breeding experiments in pure B6 mice, hemizygous offspring born to a Iap5-1full B6 parent were highly methylated and those born to a Iap5-1solo B6 parent were lowly methylated (Figure 4B).
evidence: Experimental observation from hybrid cross experiments shown in Figure 4B

claim: Hemizygous offspring born to a Iap5-1solo B6 parent were lowly methylated.
source: In line with our breeding experiments in pure B6 mice, hemizygous offspring born to a Iap5-1full B6 parent were highly methylated and those born to a Iap5-1solo B6 parent were lowly methylated (Figure 4B).
evidence: Experimental observation from hybrid cross experiments shown in Figure 4B

claim: Iap5-1solo methylation levels in BC and CB F1 hybrids were significantly higher compared to those in pure B6 individuals.
source: However, although Iap5-1solo methylation levels remained low in BC and CB F1 hybrids, they were significantly higher compared to those in pure B6 individuals (Figure 4C), suggesting that CAST-derived modifier(s) act on Iap5-1solo in trans.
evidence: Experimental observation from hybrid cross experiments shown in Figure 4C

claim: CAST-derived modifier(s) act on Iap5-1solo in trans.
source: However, although Iap5-1solo methylation levels remained low in BC and CB F1 hybrids, they were significantly higher compared to those in pure B6 individuals (Figure 4C), suggesting that CAST-derived modifier(s) act on Iap5-1solo in trans.
evidence: Inference based on the increased methylation in hybrid context

claim: CB offspring displayed higher and more variable Iap5-1solo methylation levels compared to BC offspring.
source: In addition, CB offspring displayed higher and more variable Iap5-1solo methylation levels compared to BC offspring, indicative of a genetic background-specific maternal effect similar to those recently reported at VM-IAPs (Bertozzi et al., 2020).
evidence: Experimental observation from hybrid cross experiments shown in Figure 4B

claim: There is a genetic background-specific maternal effect at Iap5-1solo.
source: In addition, CB offspring displayed higher and more variable Iap5-1solo methylation levels compared to BC offspring, indicative of a genetic background-specific maternal effect similar to those recently reported at VM-IAPs (Bertozzi et al., 2020).
evidence: Inference based on the differential methylation between reciprocal crosses

claim: N1 Iap5-1solo mice showed even higher and more variable methylation levels compared to F1 Iap5-1solo mice.
source: We further interrogated the strain-specific maternal effect by backcrossing Iap5-1solo CB hybrid males to pure CAST females. This resulted in a cumulative effect, whereby N1 Iap5-1solo mice showed even higher and more variable methylation levels compared to F1 Iap5-1solo mice (Figure 4C).
evidence: Experimental observation from backcross experiments shown in Figure 4C

claim: The CAST content of the inherited paternal genome and passage through a CAST egg may compound each other.
source: Therefore, the CAST content of the inherited paternal genome and passage through a CAST egg may compound each other.
evidence: Inference based on the cumulative effect observed in backcross experiments

claim: The subsequent N2 backcrossed generation did not cause a further increase in methylation.
source: The subsequent N2 backcrossed generation did not cause a further increase in methylation, and backcrossing N5 males to B6 females resulted in a reversion to the original B6 methylation state (Figure 4C).
evidence: Experimental observation from backcross experiments shown in Figure 4C

claim: Backcrossing N5 males to B6 females resulted in a reversion to the original B6 methylation state.
source: The subsequent N2 backcrossed generation did not cause a further increase in methylation, and backcrossing N5 males to B6 females resulted in a reversion to the original B6 methylation state (Figure 4C).
evidence: Experimental observation from backcross experiments shown in Figure 4C

claim: These results support a role for strain-specific oocyte factors (possibly polymorphic KZFPs) in driving genetic–epigenetic interactions.
source: These results are reminiscent of strain-specific behaviours of transgene methylation reported decades ago and support a role for strain-specific oocyte factors (possibly polymorphic KZFPs) in driving these genetic–epigenetic interactions (Allen et al., 1990; Bertozzi et al., 2020; Kearns et al., 2000).
evidence: Inference based on the maternal effects observed and supported by citations to Allen et al., 1990; Bertozzi et al., 2020; Kearns et al., 2000

claim: The IAPs located at the Avy and AxinFu VM-IAPs exhibit increased DNA methylation following gestational methyl supplementation.
source: The IAPs located at the Avy and AxinFu VM-IAPs exhibit increased DNA methylation following gestational methyl supplementation, resulting in shifts in the associated coat colour and tail morphology phenotypes, respectively (Waterland et al., 2006; Waterland and Jirtle, 2003).
evidence: Supported by citations to Waterland et al., 2006; Waterland and Jirtle, 2003

claim: Gestational methyl supplementation results in shifts in the associated coat colour and tail morphology phenotypes at Avy and AxinFu.
source: The IAPs located at the Avy and AxinFu VM-IAPs exhibit increased DNA methylation following gestational methyl supplementation, resulting in shifts in the associated coat colour and tail morphology phenotypes, respectively (Waterland et al., 2006; Waterland and Jirtle, 2003).
evidence: Supported by citations to Waterland et al., 2006; Waterland and Jirtle, 2003

claim: Iap5-1solo remained unmethylated in the methyl-supplemented offspring.
source: Unlike Avy and AxinFu loci, Iap5-1solo remained unmethylated in the methyl-supplemented offspring (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), indicating that complete lack of methylation at IAPs does not go hand-in-hand with susceptibility to dietary methyl supplementation.
evidence: Experimental observation from dietary intervention experiment shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1

claim: Complete lack of methylation at IAPs does not go hand-in-hand with susceptibility to dietary methyl supplementation.
source: Unlike Avy and AxinFu loci, Iap5-1solo remained unmethylated in the methyl-supplemented offspring (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), indicating that complete lack of methylation at IAPs does not go hand-in-hand with susceptibility to dietary methyl supplementation.
evidence: Inference based on the lack of response to dietary intervention

claim: Pgm2 and Rell1 expression levels in the thymus and placenta were significantly higher in Iap5-1solo than in Iap5-1full individuals.
source: Pgm2 and Rell1 expression levels in the thymus and placenta were significantly higher in Iap5-1solo than in Iap5-1full individuals, indicating that in these tissues the unmethylated solo LTR is associated with increased expression (Figure 5B).
evidence: Experimental observation from RT-qPCR shown in Figure 5B

claim: In thymus and placenta tissues, the unmethylated solo LTR is associated with increased expression of Pgm2 and Rell1.
source: Pgm2 and Rell1 expression levels in the thymus and placenta were significantly higher in Iap5-1solo than in Iap5-1full individuals, indicating that in these tissues the unmethylated solo LTR is associated with increased expression (Figure 5B).
evidence: Inference based on the correlation between methylation status and gene expression

claim: Tbc1d1 did not display significant differences in expression in any of the tested tissues.
source: Tbc1d1, the furthest in distance from Iap5-1, did not display significant differences in expression in any of the tested tissues, suggesting that proximity to the Iap5-1 locus is predictive of its transcriptional effect (Figure 5B).
evidence: Experimental observation from RT-qPCR shown in Figure 5B

claim: Proximity to the Iap5-1 locus is predictive of its transcriptional effect.
source: Tbc1d1, the furthest in distance from Iap5-1, did not display significant differences in expression in any of the tested tissues, suggesting that proximity to the Iap5-1 locus is predictive of its transcriptional effect (Figure 5B).
evidence: Inference based on the distance-dependent effect on gene expression

claim: 5830416l19Rik expression in the thymus was barely detected in Iap5-1full samples.
source: 5830416l19Rik expression in the thymus was barely detected in Iap5-1full samples, showing a highly significant increase in Iap5-1solo samples (Figure 5B).
evidence: Experimental observation from RT-qPCR shown in Figure 5B

claim: 5830416l19Rik expression in the thymus showed a highly significant increase in Iap5-1solo samples.
source: 5830416l19Rik expression in the thymus was barely detected in Iap5-1full samples, showing a highly significant increase in Iap5-1solo samples (Figure 5B).
evidence: Experimental observation from RT-qPCR shown in Figure 5B

claim: Rell1 was the only gene to show a significant difference in expression in liver tissue.
source: Rell1 was the only gene to show a significant difference in expression in liver tissue and the directionality of the effect was inversed, with lower expression levels observed in Iap5-1solo individuals (Figure 5B).
evidence: Experimental observation from RT-qPCR shown in Figure 5B

claim: In liver tissue, Rell1 expression was lower in Iap5-1solo individuals.
source: Rell1 was the only gene to show a significant difference in expression in liver tissue and the directionality of the effect was inversed, with lower expression levels observed in Iap5-1solo individuals (Figure 5B).
evidence: Experimental observation from RT-qPCR shown in Figure 5B

claim: No significant differences in expression were observed for any of the genes in cortex samples.
source: No significant differences in expression were observed for any of the genes in cortex samples (Figure 5B).
evidence: Experimental observation from RT-qPCR shown in Figure 5B

claim: Transcription of the unique non-coding regions bordering Iap5-1solo was detected in thymus and cortex.
source: In thymus and cortex, however, we detected transcription of the unique non-coding regions bordering Iap5-1solo, which was not observed for the equivalent regions bordering Iap5-1full (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Experimental observation from RT-qPCR shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1

claim: Transcription of the unique non-coding regions bordering Iap5-1full was not observed in thymus and cortex.
source: In thymus and cortex, however, we detected transcription of the unique non-coding regions bordering Iap5-1solo, which was not observed for the equivalent regions bordering Iap5-1full (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Experimental observation from RT-qPCR shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1

claim: The Iap5-1 polymorphism is associated with tissue-specific altered adjacent gene expression.
source: Together, these data show that the Iap5-1 polymorphism is associated with tissue-specific altered adjacent gene expression.
evidence: Inference based on the tissue-specific gene expression differences observed

claim: Pgm2 is the closest coding gene to Iap5-1, lying 55 kb downstream of the 3′ LTR.
source: Pgm2 is the closest coding gene to Iap5-1, lying 55 kb downstream of the 3′ LTR.
evidence: Genomic location information

claim: PGM2 catalyses the interconversion between glucose 1-phosphate and glucose 6-phosphate.
source: PGM2 catalyses the interconversion between glucose 1-phosphate and glucose 6-phosphate and has a secondary role to that of the predominant PGM isozyme, PGM1 (Geer et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Geer et al., 2010

claim: PGM2 has a secondary role to that of the predominant PGM isozyme, PGM1.
source: PGM2 catalyses the interconversion between glucose 1-phosphate and glucose 6-phosphate and has a secondary role to that of the predominant PGM isozyme, PGM1 (Geer et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Geer et al., 2010

claim: PGM1 deficiency in humans is associated with glycogen storage disease and a congenital disorder of glycosylation.
source: PGM1 deficiency in humans is associated with glycogen storage disease and a congenital disorder of glycosylation (Beamer, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Beamer, 2015

claim: PGM2 has been associated with metabolic disease in GWAS studies.
source: PGM2 has been associated with metabolic disease in GWAS studies (Timmons et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Timmons et al., 2018

claim: Fasting plasma glucose concentrations were significantly lower in Iap5-1solo mice.
source: While most assays revealed no difference between the two variants (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A), we found that fasting plasma glucose and triglyceride concentrations were significantly lower in Iap5-1solo mice (Figure 5C).
evidence: Experimental observation from metabolic assays shown in Figure 5C

claim: Fasting plasma triglyceride concentrations were significantly lower in Iap5-1solo mice.
source: While most assays revealed no difference between the two variants (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A), we found that fasting plasma glucose and triglyceride concentrations were significantly lower in Iap5-1solo mice (Figure 5C).
evidence: Experimental observation from metabolic assays shown in Figure 5C

claim: Glucose tolerance tests did not show additional metabolic disparities between the two Iap5-1 variants.
source: Glucose tolerance tests did not show additional metabolic disparities between the two variants (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Experimental observation from glucose tolerance tests shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B

claim: The emergence of a derepressed solo LTR near a gene involved in glucose metabolism has phenotypic implications.
source: These findings suggest that the emergence of a derepressed solo LTR near a gene involved in glucose metabolism has phenotypic implications, providing a basis for further functional characterisation of this model.
evidence: Inference based on the metabolic differences observed

claim: Inter-LTR recombination events have historically been identified due to phenotypic reversions of ERV-induced mutations.
source: Historically, inter-LTR recombination events have been identified due to phenotypic reversions of ERV-induced mutations, whereby the phenotypic effect of the insertion is reversed following proviral excision and solo LTR formation (Bultman et al., 1994; Seperack et al., 1988; Stoye et al., 1988).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bultman et al., 1994; Seperack et al., 1988; Stoye et al., 1988

claim: This study identified an inter-LTR recombination event based on its epigenetic rather than phenotypic outcome.
source: In this study, we identified one such chromosomal event based on its epigenetic rather than phenotypic outcome, revealing Iap5-1 as a genetically induced epiallele in the ostensibly isogenic B6 mouse strain.
evidence: Main finding of the study

claim: Iap5-1 is a genetically induced epiallele in the ostensibly isogenic B6 mouse strain.
source: In this study, we identified one such chromosomal event based on its epigenetic rather than phenotypic outcome, revealing Iap5-1 as a genetically induced epiallele in the ostensibly isogenic B6 mouse strain.
evidence: Main finding of the study

claim: The Iap5-1 locus is a valuable endogenous system to study the mechanisms, evolution, and functional implications of TE repression in both the germline and soma.
source: We demonstrated that the Iap5-1full and Iap5-1solo variants display distinct DNA and H3K9 methylation profiles which are associated with differential adjacent gene expression and altered metabolism, establishing the Iap5-1 locus as a valuable endogenous system to study the mechanisms, evolution, and functional implications of TE repression in both the germline and soma.
evidence: Conclusion based on the findings of the study

claim: The unmethylated status of Iap5-1solo sets it apart from other solo LTRs in the B6 genome.
source: The unmethylated status of Iap5-1solo sets it apart from other solo LTRs in the B6 genome, the vast majority of which (>93%) are highly methylated (Shimosuga et al., 2017).
evidence: Comparison with published data supported by citation to Shimosuga et al., 2017

claim: More than 93% of solo LTRs in the B6 genome are highly methylated.
source: The unmethylated status of Iap5-1solo sets it apart from other solo LTRs in the B6 genome, the vast majority of which (>93%) are highly methylated (Shimosuga et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Shimosuga et al., 2017

claim: Shimosuga and colleagues quantified DNA methylation at more than 8000 B6 IAP LTRs.
source: Shimosuga and colleagues quantified DNA methylation at more than 8000 B6 IAP LTRs and only 14 exhibited less than 20% methylation in tail samples.
evidence: Reference to published work by Shimosuga et al.

claim: Only 14 IAP LTRs exhibited less than 20% methylation in tail samples in the Shimosuga study.
source: Shimosuga and colleagues quantified DNA methylation at more than 8000 B6 IAP LTRs and only 14 exhibited less than 20% methylation in tail samples.
evidence: Reference to published work by Shimosuga et al.

claim: Ten of the hypomethylated IAP LTRs identified by Shimosuga were solo LTRs, mostly of the same subtype as the Iap5-1 LTR (IAPLTR2_mm).
source: Ten of these were solo LTRs, mostly of the same subtype as the Iap5-1 LTR (IAPLTR2_mm).
evidence: Reference to published work by Shimosuga et al.

claim: The authors classified the Iap5-1 LTR as a hypomethylated 3′ LTR of a full-length IAP, but in all likelihood they unknowingly detected the hypomethylated Iap5-1solo allele.
source: While the authors classified the Iap5-1 LTR as a hypomethylated 3′ LTR of a full-length IAP, in all likelihood they unknowingly detected the hypomethylated Iap5-1solo allele in their particular samples.
evidence: Inference based on the findings of the current study

claim: It is conceivable that some of the other documented hypomethylated LTRs of full-length IAPs are in fact solo LTRs formed from recent recombination events.
source: It is conceivable that some of the other documented hypomethylated LTRs of full-length IAPs are in fact solo LTRs formed from recent recombination events.
evidence: Speculation based on the findings of the current study

claim: Individual hypomethylated IAPs in either tail or sperm were non-overlapping in the Shimosuga study.
source: In comparing tail and sperm DNA methylation, the same study showed that individual hypomethylated IAPs in either tail or sperm were non-overlapping.
evidence: Reference to published work by Shimosuga et al.

claim: The non-overlapping hypomethylated IAPs in tail and sperm is consistent with the hypermethylation of Iap5-1solo in sperm.
source: This is consistent with the hypermethylation of Iap5-1solo that we observed in sperm and highlights the divergence of TE silencing mechanisms between the soma and the germline.
evidence: Inference based on comparison with published data

claim: The Iap5-1solo variant is associated with increased expression of adjacent genes in thymic and placental tissue.
source: We showed that the Iap5-1solo variant is associated with increased expression of adjacent genes in thymic and placental tissue.
evidence: Main finding of the study supported by RT-qPCR data

claim: The transcriptional consequences of the Iap5-1 polymorphism were tissue-specific.
source: The transcriptional consequences were tissue-specific: Rell1 expression was lower in Iap5-1solo compared to Iap5-1full livers, and no gene expression differences were observed in cortex samples.
evidence: Main finding of the study supported by RT-qPCR data

claim: The lncRNA 5830416l19Rik was only expressed in thymus samples collected from Iap5-1solo individuals.
source: The lncRNA 5830416l19Rik, identified from the sequencing of adult male thymus and aorta cDNA libraries (Kawai et al., 2001), was only expressed in thymus samples collected from Iap5-1solo individuals; it was nearly undetectable in Iap5-1full thymic samples and not expressed at all in any of the other tested tissues.
evidence: Experimental observation from RT-qPCR

claim: The formation of Iap5-1solo gave rise to 5830416l19Rik as a novel tissue-specific (perhaps immune-specific) lncRNA.
source: We speculate that the formation of Iap5-1solo gave rise to 5830416l19Rik as a novel tissue-specific (perhaps immune-specific) lncRNA.
evidence: Speculation based on the expression pattern observed

claim: IAP transcripts are rarely detected in somatic tissues outside of tumours and early embryogenesis, but thymic and activated splenic cells are notable exceptions.
source: Indeed, IAP transcripts are rarely detected in somatic tissues outside of tumours and early embryogenesis, but thymic and activated splenic cells are notable exceptions (Kuff and Lueders, 1988).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kuff and Lueders, 1988

claim: Young ERVs have recently been implicated in shaping the evolution of transcriptional networks underlying innate immunity.
source: In addition, young ERVs have recently been implicated in shaping the evolution of transcriptional networks underlying innate immunity (Chuong et al., 2016; Tie et al., 2018; Ye et al., 2020), and our group recently identified individual IAP elements that exhibit inter-individual methylation variability exclusively in B cells (Elmer et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Chuong et al., 2016; Tie et al., 2018; Ye et al., 2020

claim: Individual IAP elements exhibit inter-individual methylation variability exclusively in B cells.
source: In addition, young ERVs have recently been implicated in shaping the evolution of transcriptional networks underlying innate immunity (Chuong et al., 2016; Tie et al., 2018; Ye et al., 2020), and our group recently identified individual IAP elements that exhibit inter-individual methylation variability exclusively in B cells (Elmer et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work by the authors (Elmer et al., 2021)

claim: Iap5-1solo individuals exhibit lower plasma glucose and triglyceride concentrations compared to Iap5-1full individuals.
source: Along with the transcriptional differences observed at the metabolic gene Pgm2, we found that Iap5-1solo individuals exhibit lower plasma glucose and triglyceride concentrations compared to Iap5-1full individuals.
evidence: Main finding of the study supported by metabolic assays

claim: TE insertions and their epigenetic modification can have quantifiable consequences on host metabolic pathways.
source: Nevertheless, our work adds to the body of work suggesting that TE insertions and their epigenetic modification can have quantifiable consequences on host metabolic pathways (Du et al., 2016; Kuehnen et al., 2012; Scherneck et al., 2009; Yen et al., 1994).
evidence: Supported by citations to Du et al., 2016; Kuehnen et al., 2012; Scherneck et al., 2009; Yen et al., 1994

claim: Iap5-1solo is susceptible to genetic background effects, whereby passage through a CAST egg promotes methylation of the B6-derived solo LTR.
source: We have shown that Iap5-1solo is susceptible to genetic background effects, whereby passage through a CAST egg promotes methylation of the B6-derived solo LTR.
evidence: Main finding of the study supported by hybrid cross experiments

claim: KZFP diversification is associated with strain-specific IAP methylation.
source: In a recent study we reported the same effect at a number of VM-IAPs and showed that KZFP diversification is associated with strain-specific IAP methylation (Bertozzi et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work by the authors (Bertozzi et al., 2020)

claim: The differential recruitment of heterochromatin factors by KZFPs is involved in driving the epigenetic differences between Iap5-1full and Iap5-1solo.
source: This combined with the identification of candidate KZFPs capable of binding the Iap5-1 variants suggests that the differential recruitment of heterochromatin factors by KZFPs is involved in both driving the epigenetic differences between Iap5-1full and Iap5-1solo, and for the strain-specific methylation of Iap5-1solo.
evidence: Inference based on the KZFP binding data and genetic background effects

claim: The differential recruitment of heterochromatin factors by KZFPs is involved in the strain-specific methylation of Iap5-1solo.
source: This combined with the identification of candidate KZFPs capable of binding the Iap5-1 variants suggests that the differential recruitment of heterochromatin factors by KZFPs is involved in both driving the epigenetic differences between Iap5-1full and Iap5-1solo, and for the strain-specific methylation of Iap5-1solo.
evidence: Inference based on the KZFP binding data and genetic background effects

claim: The wide range of methylation levels observed at the Iap5-1solo allele across genetically identical CB individuals renders this locus a bona fide VM-IAP in this hybrid context.
source: In fact, by definition, the wide range of methylation levels observed at the Iap5-1solo allele across genetically identical CB individuals renders this locus a bona fide VM-IAP (or metastable epiallele) in this hybrid context (Bertozzi and Ferguson-Smith, 2020; Rakyan et al., 2002).
evidence: Inference based on the definition of VM-IAPs and the observed methylation variability

claim: The new Iap5-1solo variant is expected to be a useful tool for the study of epigenetic stochasticity in the absence of genetic variation.
source: Therefore, we expect the new Iap5-1solo variant to be a useful tool for the study of epigenetic stochasticity in the absence of genetic variation, a phenomenon for which the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood.
evidence: Speculation about future utility based on the findings

claim: The identification of Iap5-1solo demonstrates that cryptic genetic diversity in an inbred mouse population can have functional repercussions with important implications for experimental outcomes.
source: The identification of Iap5-1solo demonstrates that cryptic genetic diversity in an inbred mouse population can have functional repercussions with important implications for experimental outcomes.
evidence: Conclusion based on the findings of the study

claim: The current mouse reference genome harbours large gaps and inaccuracies, largely due to mapping difficulties associated with the repeat genome.
source: We are reminded that the current mouse reference genome harbours large gaps and inaccuracies, largely due to mapping difficulties associated with the repeat genome.
evidence: General knowledge about limitations of reference genomes

claim: Inter-LTR recombination events are an underappreciated source of genetic variation.
source: Inter-LTR recombination events are surely an underappreciated source of genetic variation considering that a lack of uniquely mapped reads in internal portions of TEs is more likely to be attributed to technical rather than biological limitations.
evidence: Inference based on the findings and technical limitations

claim: A recent study in humans developed a computational pipeline to capture dimorphic human ERVs (HERVs) resulting from inter-LTR recombination events and detected dozens of previously unidentified candidates.
source: A recent study in humans developed a computational pipeline to capture dimorphic human ERVs (HERVs) resulting from inter-LTR recombination events and detected dozens of previously unidentified candidates (Thomas et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Thomas et al., 2018

claim: The advent of analytical tools and routine long-read sequencing of whole genomes will be highly beneficial in addressing issues with TE mapping.
source: The advent of such analytical tools as well as routine long-read sequencing of whole genomes will be highly beneficial in addressing these issues.
evidence: Speculation about future technological solutions
